description: Break down news coverage volume over time by source language or source country, returning a multi-series time series (one series per language or country). Shows which countries or languages drove early vs. late coverage — useful for tracing how a story propagated geographically or across language communities. Returns the top 10 series ranked by the sum of their values and names every other series under otherSeriesLabels — pass any labels, ranked or not, as the series input to get only those series, complete. A response carries as many whole series as fit its size budget; when more remain it returns nextOffset — pass it back as offset with otherwise identical inputs for the next page. Values are normalized: each point is the topic's share of that source's media output, not an absolute article count, so values from different sources do not add up to a share. Small media markets with concentrated coverage therefore rank above large markets with diverse output — a high value means the topic dominated that source's coverage, not that it published the most articles. Use breakdownBy "country" with the signal-detection chain to map geographic attention, or "language" to detect non-English media surges.

breakdownBy.description: Breakdown dimension: "language" for source language time series, "country" for source country time series.

endDatetime.description: End datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20240131235959). Must pair with startDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected.

offset.description: Zero-based series offset — into the ranked top 10, or into the series named in series. Pass nextOffset from the preceding response, with otherwise identical inputs, to get the next page.

query.description: Search query using GDELT syntax. Same operators as gdelt_search_articles: phrases, boolean OR, sourcecountry:, sourcelang:, domain:, theme: (GKG theme identifiers come from gdelt_search_themes).

series.description: Exact series labels to return instead of the ranked overview, e.g. ["Portuguese", "Vietnamese"]. Take them verbatim from otherSeriesLabels or topSeries[].label in a response, or from the label list an unknown_series error prints. Each one comes back complete under selectedSeries, in the order requested; a label that matches nothing is rejected rather than silently skipped. Omit to get the ranked overview.

startDatetime.description: Start datetime in GDELT format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS — exactly 14 digits, no separators (e.g. 20240101000000). Must pair with endDatetime; supplying only one of the two is rejected.

timespan.description: Time window relative to now, minimum "15min"; other examples: "24h", "7d", "1m". Ignored when startDatetime/endDatetime are set. Maximum 3 months.

name: gdelt_get_coverage_breakdown

breakdownBy.description: Breakdown dimension used for this response.

dateResolution.description: Temporal resolution of data points — 15min, hour, or day — inferred from the spacing of the returned timesteps. Omitted when fewer than two distinct timesteps came back.

effectiveQuery.description: Echoed query string for use in follow-up calls.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `unknown_series`: A label passed in the series input matches no series in a non-empty breakdown. `offset_out_of_range`: The requested offset is at or beyond the last series of a non-empty overview (the top 10), or of the series named in series. `invalid_date_range`: Only one of startDatetime / endDatetime was supplied, one of them is not a real UTC calendar timestamp, or startDatetime is not earlier than endDatetime. `invalid_query`: GDELT rejected the query string as malformed — bad keyword length, unbalanced parentheses, or an illegal character. `gdelt_rate_limited`: GDELT rejected the request for its one-request-per-five-seconds limit, or too many requests were already queued for this one to start in time. `gdelt_unavailable`: GDELT DOC API is unreachable or temporarily returned no usable data. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

nextOffset.description: Offset of the next page, for the same inputs. Absent when this page reaches the last series.

notice.description: Guidance when the query matched no coverage in the window — how to broaden the query or extend the window — or, when this response is one page of several, which series it returned out of how many. Absent when every series fit in one response.

otherSeriesLabels.description: Label of every series beyond the top 10, ranked by the sum of its values, on every overview page. Pass any of them to the series input to retrieve that series' complete data. Omitted when all series fit in the top 10, or when the series input selects series instead.

selectedSeries.description: Complete, untruncated time series for the labels requested via the series input — those of this page, in the order requested. Omitted when series was not supplied.

items.description: A single language or country coverage series.

data.description: Time-ordered data points for this series.

items.description: A single data point for this series.

value.description: Normalized coverage volume at this timestep — the topic's share of this source's media output, not an absolute article count.

label.description: Series label (language name or country name).

topSeries.description: The ranked overview: the top 10 series by the sum of their values, those of this page in rank order. Omitted when the series input selects series instead.

totalCount.description: Total number of series GDELT returned, before ranking into the top 10 or paging.
